- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to be too low in the middle of the horizon, then gradually increases — suggesting a lag in capturing upward momentum.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 71+), model overreacts and overshoots in the immediate next period, then corrects.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to pull prices back toward historical averages when they deviate significantly.
- Forecast horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts are systematically too low, especially when true values are rising or volatile.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of late-period spikes (e.g., 72–73 range) and fails to anticipate them until 1–2 days before occurrence.
- Model exhibits “early dip” behavior — predicts a drop early, then fails to recover, missing upward trends that emerge mid-horizon.
